meta.title: "If you're not with us, you're the enemy" — how to teach your child to withstand group pressure | Sila Slova
meta.description: Teach your child to see "us vs them" pressure, refuse imposed roles and keep the right not to pick extremes. Game-based course for children aged 10–16.

hero.headline: "You're either with us or against us" — and your child picks a side just to stay in the group?
hero.subheadline: "If you don't support us, you're a traitor", "everyone normal has already chosen". There's no room for their own view — only "one of us" or "the enemy". Your child is reacting to the fear of being rejected.

media.alt: A child pulled into choosing a side between two camps of peers

pain.title: "One of us" or "the enemy" — and no room for your own view
pain.body:
Your child is forced to pick a side. "You're either with us or against us", "if you don't support us you're a traitor", "everyone normal has already chosen" — at school, in their group, in chats. The child feels the pressure and chooses, just to avoid being pushed out of the group.

But this isn't a position — it's group pressure. The child is forced to take a side even when the situation is more complicated. And emotion is added on top — "friend/enemy", "us/them". The choice is squeezed into two extremes when there are really more.

Without the skill to spot it, the child agrees just to stay "inside". The result — they give up their own view in exchange for acceptance. Not because they "cave", but because they're reacting to the fear of being rejected.

solution.title: "Sila Slova" — a detective drama that teaches critical thinking
solution.body: 50 episodes, 13 critical thinking lessons. Your child plays — but is actually learning to defend themselves with words.
bullets: 🔍 Sees the "with us or against us" pressure and refuses the imposed role
🧠 Understands: "us/them" is emotion, not a real choice
💬 Keeps the right not to pick extremes
🛡️ Can not be "against" even when they're not "for"

social_proof.quote: She used to immediately take someone's side just to avoid being left alone. Now she says "I'm not against you, but I think my own way" — and won't let herself be dragged into camps.
social_proof.author: Tetiana, mum of 12-year-old Alina

faq.q: Is it a game or a learning course?
faq.a: Both at the same time. "Sila Slova" looks like a detective series, but every episode contains a hidden critical thinking lesson.

faq.q: What age is it suitable for?
faq.a: Ideal for 10–16 year olds. At this age, children are receptive to new thinking patterns and are still forming their views.

faq.q: How much time is needed each day?
faq.a: 15–20 minutes per episode. Flexible schedule — your child can come back at any convenient time.

faq.q: Is registration required for the demo?
faq.a: No. The demo episode is fully open — no registration, no subscription, no personal data required.
